title: Eventual isomorphism of a graded map from its standard localizations
statement: Let $S=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}S_d$ be a nonnegatively graded commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and suppose $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in S_1$ generate $S$ as an $S_0$-algebra, with $r\ge0$. Let $M=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}M_n$ and $N=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}N_n$ be $S$-modules with $S_aM_b\subseteq M_{a+b}$ and $S_aN_b\subseteq N_{a+b}$. Let $\psi:M\to N$ be $S$-linear and degree-preserving. Assume that $M$ and $N^+=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}N_n$ are finitely generated as $S$-modules [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. For a graded module $T$, let $T_{(f_i)}\subseteq T_{f_i}$ consist of fractions $x/f_i^a$ with $a\ge0$ and $x\in T_a$, with the ordinary localization equivalence relation [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away, def-sc-degree-zero-module-fractions]. Suppose each induced map $\psi_{(f_i)}:M_{(f_i)}\to N_{(f_i)}$, $x/f_i^a\mapsto\psi(x)/f_i^a$, is an isomorphism. Set $M^+=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}M_n$ and let $\psi^+:M^+\to N^+$ be the restriction. Then $K=\ker\psi^+$ and $Q=N^+/\psi^+(M^+)$, with the induced gradings, are finite graded $S$-modules with $K_{(f_i)}=Q_{(f_i)}=0$ for every $i$. For each $T\in\{K,Q\}$ there are finite homogeneous generators $t_j\in T_{e_j}$ with $e_j\ge0$ and integers $b_{ij}\ge1$ satisfying $f_i^{b_{ij}}t_j=0$; for any such generators and exponents, $T_n=0$ whenever $n>B_T=\max(\{0\}\cup\{e_j+\sum_{i=1}^r b_{ij}:j\})$. In particular, for $n_0=1+\max(B_K,B_Q)\ge0$, every $\psi_n:M_n\to N_n$ with $n\ge n_0$ is an $S_0$-linear isomorphism. Empty generating families and zero modules are allowed; no finiteness assumption is imposed on the negative-degree truncation of $N$.

source.place: Tag 0AG7, lemma-recover-tail-graded-module, proof: second half, from finiteness of the nonnegative kernel and cokernel through truncation invariance and the final homogeneous-generator annihilator/monomial bound; original steps 5--8. This is the abstract graded-module argument, with no sheaf or Proj hypothesis.

proof.text: The nonnegative pieces $M^+$ and $N^+$ are $S$-submodules: multiplying a component of degree $b\ge0$ by a scalar of degree $a\ge0$ has degree $a+b\ge0$. Degree preservation restricts $\psi$ to $\psi^+$. If $\sum_n x_n$ lies in its kernel, then $\sum_n\psi(x_n)=0$ and uniqueness of homogeneous components gives $\psi(x_n)=0$ for every $n$. Its image is homogeneous too, since the component of degree $n$ of $\psi^+(x)$ is $\psi(x_n)$. Thus $K$ inherits the componentwise kernel grading, and $Q$ has components $Q_n=N_n/\psi(M_n)$ for $n\ge0$, with zero components for $n<0$: projecting any representative to degree $n$ gives the quotient projection, and the homogeneous image makes these projections well defined. These descriptions also prove the required compatibility of scalar multiplication with the gradings.

source.place: Tag 0AG7, lemma-recover-tail-graded-module, proof: nonnegative kernel and cokernel, truncation invariance, and final homogeneous-generator argument (lines 3901–3929).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] to the submodules $M^+\subseteq M$ and $K\subseteq M$: $S$ is Noetherian and $M$ is finite by hypothesis, so both are finite. The quotient $Q$ is finite because the images of any finite generating family of $N^+$ generate $Q$, directly by [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Hence both kernel and cokernel are finite graded modules, without using any finiteness of $N$ itself.

source.place: Tag 0AG7, lemma-recover-tail-graded-module, proof: nonnegative kernel and cokernel, truncation invariance, and final homogeneous-generator argument (lines 3901–3929).

proof.text: Fix $i$. Inclusion induces isomorphisms $(M^+)_{(f_i)}\to M_{(f_i)}$ and $(N^+)_{(f_i)}\to N_{(f_i)}$. Every degree-zero fraction has numerator in degree $a\ge0$ and denominator $f_i^a$, so its numerator already lies in the nonnegative truncation [def-sc-degree-zero-module-fractions]. Two such fractions are equal precisely when some power of $f_i$ kills their cross-multiplied difference [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]; this is the same equation in the submodule as in the ambient module. For $x\in T_a$ and $y\in T_b$, their sum is $(f_i^b x+f_i^a y)/f_i^{a+b}$; its numerator has degree $a+b\ge0$ in either truncation or ambient module. Likewise a degree-zero scalar $s/f_i^c$, $s\in S_c$, acts by $sx/f_i^{a+c}$, whose numerator has degree $a+c\ge0$. Thus the bijections preserve the module operations. They commute with the maps induced by $\psi$ because both composites send $x/f_i^a$ to $\psi(x)/f_i^a$. Hence $(\psi^+)_{(f_i)}$ is an isomorphism by the hypothesis on $\psi_{(f_i)}$.

source.place: Tag 0AG7, lemma-recover-tail-graded-module, proof: nonnegative kernel and cokernel, truncation invariance, and final homogeneous-generator argument (lines 3901–3929).

proof.text: Extend the grading on $S$ to $\mathbf Z$ by $S_a=0$ for $a<0$, and use the gradings of step 1. The sequence $0\to K\to M^+\xrightarrow{\psi^+}N^+\to Q\to0$ is exact with degree-preserving maps, and $f_i$ has degree $1\ge0$. Apply [lem-sc-graded-localization-exact] to each consecutive triple, including the zero endpoints; its statement explicitly includes finite exact sequences. The localization of the zero module is zero directly from its fraction description. This gives an exact sequence $0\to K_{(f_i)}\to(M^+)_{(f_i)}\xrightarrow{(\psi^+)_{(f_i)}}(N^+)_{(f_i)}\to Q_{(f_i)}\to0$. The middle arrow is bijective by step 3. At $K_{(f_i)}$ exactness makes its map to $(M^+)_{(f_i)}$ injective, while exactness at $(M^+)_{(f_i)}$ makes its image zero; hence $K_{(f_i)}=0$. At $(N^+)_{(f_i)}$ the quotient map is zero because the middle arrow is surjective, and exactness at $Q_{(f_i)}$ makes that zero map surjective; hence $Q_{(f_i)}=0$.

source.place: Tag 0AG7, lemma-recover-tail-graded-module, proof: nonnegative kernel and cokernel, truncation invariance, and final homogeneous-generator argument (lines 3901–3929).

proof.text: For either $T=K$ or $T=Q$, choose finite generators $g_1,\ldots,g_s$ using [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Decompose each $g_h$ into its finitely many homogeneous components, and take the union of those finite families. Their $S$-span contains every $g_h$, hence is $T$, and each component already belongs to $T$. Omitting zero components gives finite homogeneous generators $t_j\in T_{e_j}$. All $e_j\ge0$, since $T$ is concentrated in nonnegative degrees by step 1. If $T=0$, take the empty family.

source.place: Tag 0AG7, lemma-recover-tail-graded-module, proof: nonnegative kernel and cokernel, truncation invariance, and final homogeneous-generator argument (lines 3901–3929).

proof.text: For each $i,j$, the fraction $t_j/f_i^{e_j}$ is in $T_{(f_i)}$ because numerator and denominator have the same degree [def-sc-degree-zero-module-fractions]. It is zero by step 4. Comparing it to $0/1$ in the equivalence relation of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] gives $f_i^k(1\cdot t_j-f_i^{e_j}\cdot0)=0$ for some $k\ge0$, hence $f_i^k t_j=0$. Set $b_{ij}=\max(1,k)$; multiplication by the additional power gives $f_i^{b_{ij}}t_j=0$ and $b_{ij}\ge1$. There is no division by $f_i$ inside $T$, so this also applies to zero and nilpotent $f_i$.

source.place: Tag 0AG7, lemma-recover-tail-graded-module, proof: nonnegative kernel and cokernel, truncation invariance, and final homogeneous-generator argument (lines 3901–3929).

proof.text: Now fix ANY finite homogeneous generating family $t_j\in T_{e_j}$ and ANY annihilating exponents $b_{ij}\ge1$ as in the statement. For $x\in T_n$, write $x=\sum_j s_jt_j$ and expand each scalar as a polynomial over $S_0$ in the $f_i$, which is possible by the assumed algebra generation. Each resulting term is $c\prod_i f_i^{a_i}t_j$ with $c\in S_0$ and $a_i\ge0$, and is homogeneous of degree $e_j+\sum_i a_i$. Project this finite equality to degree $n$: terms with a different degree vanish under that projection, so $x$ is a sum only of such terms satisfying $\sum_i a_i=n-e_j$. This argument is simply expansion of a finite polynomial and uniqueness of homogeneous components; it requires neither algebraic independence of the $f_i$ nor a homogeneous presentation of the relations.

source.place: Tag 0AG7, lemma-recover-tail-graded-module, proof: nonnegative kernel and cokernel, truncation invariance, and final homogeneous-generator argument (lines 3901–3929).

proof.text: If $r>0$ and $n>B_T$, every retained term of step 7 has $\sum_i a_i=n-e_j>\sum_i b_{ij}$. Thus some $a_i\ge b_{ij}$ (otherwise $\sum_i a_i\le\sum_i(b_{ij}-1)<\sum_i b_{ij}$). Factoring out $f_i^{b_{ij}}$ makes that term zero. Hence $T_n=0$. If $r=0$, the only polynomial monomial is the empty product, of degree $0$, so a retained term would require $n=e_j$, impossible when $n>B_T\ge e_j$. If the generating family is empty, $T=0$ and $B_T=0$. These cases establish the stated bound with $\max(\{0\}\cup\{e_j+\sum_i b_{ij}:j\})$ for every permitted family and choice of exponents.

source.place: Tag 0AG7, lemma-recover-tail-graded-module, proof: nonnegative kernel and cokernel, truncation invariance, and final homogeneous-generator argument (lines 3901–3929).

proof.text: Take the generators and exponents obtained in steps 5–6 for $K,Q$, and let $n_0=1+\max(B_K,B_Q)$. If $n\ge n_0$, then $n\ge0$ and both $K_n=0$ and $Q_n=0$ by step 8. By the component descriptions of step 1, $K_n=0$ makes $\psi_n$ injective and $Q_n=0$ makes it surjective. Write $v:N_n\to M_n$ for its inverse as a bijection. For $y,z\in N_n$ and $a\in S_0$, applying the injective map $\psi_n$ to $v(y+z)$ and $v(y)+v(z)$ gives $y+z$ in both cases; applying it to $v(ay)$ and $av(y)$ gives $ay$ in both cases. Thus $v$ is additive and $S_0$-linear, proving the asserted $S_0$-linear isomorphism for every $n\ge n_0$.
